fields.label: Sales sourcing (services and intangibles)
fields.value: Minnesota uses market-based sourcing rather than cost of performance for services and intangibles. Receipts from services are attributed to Minnesota if received in the state, and intangible property receipts are sourced based on the purchaser's use in the state.
fields.quote: (h) Royalties and other income received for the use of or for the privilege of using intangible property, including patents, know-how, formulas, designs, processes, patterns, copyrights, trade names, service names, franchises, licenses, contracts, customer lists, or similar items, must be attributed to the state in which the property is used by the purchaser.

fields.label: Special industry rules
fields.value: Special rules apply to financial institutions, investment companies, mutual fund management services, air carriers, and athletic teams. Financial institutions apportion net income using specific receipts factor rules, while air carriers follow a dedicated formula prescribed by administrative rule.
fields.quote: Determination of receipts factor for financial institutions.

fields.label: Forms
fields.value: Apportionment is computed on Schedule M4A for C corporations filing Form M4, Schedule M8A for S corporations filing Form M8, and Schedule M3A for partnerships filing Form M3. Estates and trusts use Schedule M2NM, while tax-exempt organizations with UBIT use Schedule M4NPA.

fields.label: P.L. 86-272
fields.value: P.L. 86-272 protects businesses from tax based on net income if activities are limited to taking orders for sales of tangible personal property approved and filled from outside Minnesota. Qualifying protected entities without an independent filing requirement are not subject to the Minnesota minimum fee.
fields.quote: (a) A person is not subject to tax under this chapter if the person is engaged in the business of selling tangible personal property and taxation of that person under this chapter is precluded by Public Law 86-272, United States Code, title 15, sections 381 to 384, or would be so precluded except for the fact that the person stored tangible personal property in a state licensed facility under chapter 231.

fields.label: Sales and use tax
fields.value: Minnesota's state general sales and use tax rate is 6.875%. Local jurisdictions add local sales and use taxes on top of the state rate.
fields.quote: 1, reducing the general sales and use tax rate to 6.425%, retaining the cigarette sales tax rate of 6.875%, and expanding the sales and use tax base.

fields.label: Other notable business taxes
fields.value: Minnesota imposes a 1.8% gross revenues tax on health care providers, hospitals, surgical centers, and wholesale drug distributors.
fields.quote: 1.8% of gross revenues for health care providers, hospitals, surgical centers, and wholesale drug distributors.

fields.label: Composite returns
fields.value: Eligible nonresident individual owners with no other Minnesota-source income may elect to have the pass-through entity file composite income tax on their behalf. The tax is calculated at the highest individual income tax rate of 9.85% on Minnesota-source distributive income.
fields.source_citation: 2025 KPI, Partner's Share of Income, Credits and Modifications
fields.quote: If you elected composite income tax, the amount paid on your behalf equals 9.85% of your Minnesota source distributive income on line 53, minus your share of any credits on lines 23-25, 27-32, and 34.

fields.label: Withholding and estimated payments
fields.value: Pass-through entities must make estimated payments if their combined liability is $500 or more, paying the lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax in four equal installments. Nonresident withholding of 9.85% applies to nonresident owners with Minnesota-source distributive income of $1,000 or more unless PTE tax or composite tax is elected or Form AWC is filed.
fields.quote: Estimated Tax Payments An S corporation must make quarterly estimated tax payments if the sum of its estimated S corporation taxes, minimum fee, nonresident withholding, pass-through entity tax, and composite income tax for all nonresident shareholders electing to participate in composite income tax, less any credits, is $500 or more.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.value: Primary returns include Form M1 for individuals, Form M4 for corporations, Form M3 for partnerships, and Form M8 for S corporations. Pass-through entities also file Schedules KPI, KPC, KS, PTE, and PTE-RP as applicable.
fields.quote: Forms Which Form Should You File? Most corporations, other than S corporations, file Form M4, Corporation Franchise Tax Return.
